against the cited source and given one of three verdicts.
true-positive  - a real defect, or a warning a reviewer would defend.
false-positive - the code is correct (or the severity is not defensible);
`guard` names the documented guard that should have
caught it, so the fix has an address.
unsure         - the reviewer could not settle it from the source alone.
`state` exists so the file is a ratchet rather than a permanent red light:
open  - the analyzer still produces this false positive. `check` lists it
and does not fail on it (pass --strict to make it fail).
fixed - the analyzer no longer produces it. If it ever comes back,
`check` fails: that is the regression half of the ratchet.
A high finding whose key is absent from this file always fails `check` -
nobody has read it yet, and an unread high finding is the one thing this
corpus exists to stop.
Keys are `repo|CODE|repo-relative file|symbol`, so they survive an edit
above the finding and do not depend on which target happened to find it.
